repository.name: gothinkster/rails-realworld-example-app
repository.workload: Not supplied — a public RealWorld reference implementation with no stated production traffic.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from a real, live independent blind-pass run (not narrated in docs/evaluation.md — that document predates this schema) performed specifically to validate the measurement system end to end after the 1.0.0 milestone. Ruby on Rails had never been independently blind-passed in this project's evaluation history before this run, unlike Go/Python/JVM/Rust/.NET/Node.js. This is the first ground-truth file built directly from a raw agent review's JSON output rather than from prose already treated as established — two of its four expected findings (PERF-002's unbounded-limit shape, PERF-003's SQLite-in-production concern) and its one adjacent finding were spot-verified directly against the cloned repository's source before being accepted here, specifically the self-referential has_many claim (confirmed verbatim in app/models/article.rb) and the unclamped params[:limit] || 20 pattern (confirmed verbatim in app/controllers/articles_controller.rb). This run also serves as an E4 (zero-findings repository) attempt; it did not succeed — four real findings were produced — consistent with docs/evaluation.md §3.7's finding that no repository reviewed in this project's history has produced a literal zero-finding result.

expected.mechanism: The article and comment JSON serializers call three per-item accessors (tag_list, favorited?, following?) that each issue their own database query per item in a list, instead of being batched once across the collection — the same per-item-query-in-a-render-path shape as the N+1 patterns found in every other RealWorld implementation blind-passed in this project (Go, Python, JVM, Rust, .NET, Node.js all have an equivalent finding).

articles#index and #feed accept a caller-supplied limit with no enforced maximum (params[:limit] || 20 — a default applied only when absent, not a clamp), and comments#index applies no pagination at all. Verified verbatim against the controller source: `.limit(params[:limit] || 20)`.

SQLite is configured for production with a 5-connection pool, but SQLite allows exactly one writer to the database file at a time — the connection pool does not deliver the write concurrency its size implies, and with no WAL mode configured, writes also block concurrent reads. The same SQLite-single-writer-versus-pool-size mismatch found in spring-boot-realworld.json and gin-realworld.json, now confirmed in a third, independent stack.
config.log_level = :debug is set for the production environment — the most verbose Rails log level, applied unconditionally on every request rather than the common :info/:warn default for production.
